judge_assessment.explanation: The hard failure is confirmed on all three cited problems and understates the extent. Problem 5 says 'The area model below is one square metre cut into hundredths; use it to explain why the answer is a small fraction of a square metre' and verify.json id 5 is a single `eval` -> 0.1. Problem 7 says 'Write < or > between them, and explain your reasoning in one sentence using the words smaller than one' and id 7 asserts only the relation. Problem 9 says 'Use estimation to explain, in one sentence, why 4.9 cannot be correct' and id 9 asserts only 0.49. No manual entry exists in the file and the delivery claims '19 verified, 0 manual'. Beyond those three, six more problems print responses no entry covers: problem 1 supplies a place-value chart to fill in; problem 2 asks the student to 'Explain which way the digits shift and why the answer must be smaller than 4.5'; problem 3 asks for the product 'first in tenths ... and then as a decimal'; problem 4 asks the student to 'State the two rounded measurements you used' (7 and 4), which is machine-checkable and unasserted; problem 6 asks the student to 'rewrite both lengths in tenths, then divide'; problem 8 asks to 'Show the division in tenths'. So nine of ten problems have at least one uncovered printed response, not three. The judge's minor delivery note is also right - final_response.md says '~4 pages' and pdfinfo reports 5 - and I found one more defect the judge missed: Quick Answer 7 prints an em-dash for the verified '<' because render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies the relation string and falls back. Every value I recomputed (124 g, 0.45 m, 2.4 L, 28 m^2, 0.1 m^2, 8 pieces, '<', 0.8 kg, 0.49 m^2, 24 cups, 1.4 L) is correct.

strengths_to_preserve: answer_unit is declared on seven problems (g, m, L, m^2, kg) and bound in both directions - the worksheet's answer blank prints the unit and the key's boxed answer must repeat it - so on a decimals sheet a right number in the wrong unit cannot pass. That is the correct guard for a representations-and-applications task with explicit givens and units.

Problem 9's trap is the error written as arithmetic: 1.4 * 0.35 * 10 -> 4.9, the decimal point one place too far right. The number in Sam's stem is therefore generated by the misconception it represents rather than typed, so stem, key and trap block cannot drift.

Problem 7 attacks the multiplication-makes-bigger belief head-on by asking the student to decide between 0.6 x 12 and 12 / 0.6 WITHOUT computing either, and it is typed as a `compare` relation rather than as two evals - the check matches what the student is asked to do.

Problem 10's two parts each get their own answer blank and their own entry: 8.4/0.35 -> 24 cups and 8.4 - 0.35*20 -> 1.4 L. The second part uses a different operation on the same context, so part (a) cannot carry part (b).

The place-value chart in problem 1 is scoped to that problem's digits (1, 2, 4 in the ones, tenths and hundredths columns) and the shared how-to-work box carries no problem's numbers, so displays and givens stay separated.

root_causes.description: Three problems require a written explanation or an explanation built on a printed model, and all three are recorded as machine-verified, so a sheet whose stated method is 'show the place-value thinking, not just the algorithm' reports zero items needing a human read. The explanation is the assessed response on this focus, and the numeric check beside it is treated as covering it.
evidence: Worksheet problem 5: '... use it to explain why the answer is a small fraction of a square metre.' - verify.json id 5 is one `eval` -> 0.1.
Worksheet problem 7: '... explain your reasoning in one sentence using the words smaller than one.' - id 7 is one `compare` -> '<'.
Worksheet problem 9: 'Use estimation to explain, in one sentence, why 4.9 cannot be correct.' - id 9 is one `eval` -> 0.49.
Worksheet problem 2 adds a fourth: 'Explain which way the digits shift and why the answer must be smaller than 4.5.' - id 2 is one `eval` -> 0.45.
verify.json contains no manual entry; final_response.md states '19 verified, 0 manual'.

root_causes.description: The sheet's place-value reasoning is printed as required intermediate responses - the product in tenths, the two rounded measurements, both lengths rewritten in tenths, the division in tenths, the filled place-value chart - and none of them is asserted, because coverage is measured per problem id. Those intermediates are exactly the requested focus; the terminal decimals are the part a student could get right by algorithm alone.
evidence: Worksheet problem 4: 'State the two rounded measurements you used.' (7 m and 4 m) - verify.json id 4 asserts only the estimate 28.
Worksheet problem 3: 'Write the product first in tenths ... and then as a decimal.' - id 3 asserts only 2.4.
Worksheet problem 6: 'rewrite both lengths in tenths, then divide' (48 tenths by 6 tenths) - id 6 asserts only 8.
Worksheet problem 8: 'Show the division in tenths.' (72 tenths by 9) - id 8 asserts only 0.8.
Worksheet problem 1 prints an empty place-value chart row to complete; id 1 asserts only 124.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt has no branch for relation strings, so problem 7's verified '<' prints as the em-dash reserved for manual-only ids and the grader sees an unavailable answer for a machine-checked one.
evidence: Answer key Quick Answers block prints an em-dash for entry 7 while verify.json id 7 declares expected '<'.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt returns the em-dash when sympy.sympify raises, and sympify('<') raises.
The same defect appears in curr-119 (problem 5) and curr-125 (problems 3, 5, 8 and 11).

root_causes.description: The delivery estimates the worksheet length instead of quoting the compiled value, so the response says approximately four pages for a five-page document.
evidence: pdfinfo worksheet.pdf reports Pages: 5; machine_observation.worksheet_pages is 5.

improvements.title: Record explanation, diagnosis and drawn-representation responses as manual instead of machine-verified
improvements.proposed_change: Add the open-response cue gate and require a manual companion whenever a stem contains 'explain', 'why', 'in one sentence' or asks the student to reason from a printed model. On curr-138 problems 2, 5, 7 and 9 gain companions beside their numeric checks, the build exits 2 with four manual items, and the delivery reports the honest split instead of '19 verified, 0 manual'.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: curr-138's problem 9 stem ('Use estimation to explain, in one sentence, why 4.9 cannot be correct') with only its `eval` -> 0.49 entry must fail the gate and name problem 9; adding a manual companion must let it pass with exit 2. It passes with exit 0 today.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes this case's hard failure and the run's second-largest cluster (36 cases). The user is told which four items need reading rather than being told none do.
improvements.risk: More manual items means more human review. Correct for this content, and the manual desc should state what a full-credit explanation contains so the review stays fast.

improvements.title: Require one verification entry (or a manual companion) per printed answer slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Apply the per-slot rule so the place-value intermediates this sheet exists to teach are asserted: id 4 gains checks for the two rounded measurements (7 and 4), id 3 gains the product in tenths (24 tenths), id 6 gains both lengths rewritten in tenths (48 and 6), id 8 gains 72 tenths divided by 9, and id 1 gains the chart's shifted digit positions. Each is a plain `eval`; none needs a new verification type.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a problem declaring "slots": 3 for 'state the two rounded measurements, then the estimate' supplied with only the estimate; assert verify.py exits 1 naming the two uncovered slots. Today it exits 0.
improvements.expected_impact: Moves verification onto the requested focus - place-value reasoning - rather than the terminal decimal, and closes nine of ten problems' coverage holes on this sheet.
improvements.risk: Longer verification files and more places for an author to state an intermediate incorrectly. The generator already computes these values for the answer key, so the exposure is small.

improvements.title: Print the relation symbol for compare-type answers in the Quick Answers bank instead of an em-dash
improvements.proposed_change: Map the relation vocabulary to rendered symbols in _fmt before the sympify attempt, keeping the em-dash for manual-only ids. Problem 7's bank entry then prints the '<' symbol.
improvements.regression_test: Unit test asserting a `compare` relation entry with expected '<' renders the relation symbol in the bank; it renders an em-dash today.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores the one missing bank answer here and five more across curr-119 and curr-125.
improvements.risk: Minimal - a lookup ahead of an existing fallback.

improvements.title: Generate the delivery response's page counts from the compiled PDFs instead of writing them by hand
improvements.proposed_change: Emit measured page counts from the page-budget gate into gate_log.txt and require the delivery to quote them, so '~4 pages' becomes '5 pages'.
improvements.regression_test: Assert gate_log.txt carries a PAGES line with the compiled counts; it does not today.
improvements.expected_impact: Fixes a repeated delivery-accuracy defect across the shard.
improvements.risk: Very low; log and response text only.

case_summary: Strong decimals content - every value and unit correct, units bound in both directions on seven problems, problem 7 attacking multiplication-makes-bigger without computation, problem 9's trap generated from the misconception itself - rejected on the trust boundary. Three problems ask for an explanation or for reasoning from a printed model and all three are counted as machine-verified in a '19 verified, 0 manual' delivery. Checking beyond the judge's list, nine of the ten problems print at least one uncovered response: the product in tenths, the two rounded measurements, both lengths rewritten in tenths, the division in tenths and the place-value chart are precisely the place-value reasoning the task asked for, and none is asserted. Two smaller defects: the delivery calls the worksheet about four pages when it is five, and Quick Answer 7 prints an em-dash for the verified '<'.
